karat_reference.label: 10K (common U.S. market minimum — not a legal floor since the 2018 Guides revision)
karat_reference.durability_profile: Hardest alloy (58.33% alloy metals); resists scratching well; pale yellow hue; the usual lowest karat sold in the U.S. market, but NOT a legal minimum: the 2018 revision of 16 CFR Part 23 removed the old 10-karat threshold, and 16 CFR 23.3(c)(1) itself gives '9 Karat Gold' as an acceptable description. 10-karat is a floor for plating fineness only (23.3(c)(2)-(3), 23.4(b)).

karat_reference.label: 14K Engagement Standard
karat_reference.durability_profile: Industry benchmark balance of fine gold (58.33%) and prong strength for daily-wear engagement rings.

karat_reference.label: 18K High-Purity Fine Bridal
karat_reference.durability_profile: Rich warm saturation (75.00% pure gold); slightly softer than 14K — check prong gauge or pair with platinum/14K head on high-profile solitaires.

karat_reference.label: 22K Heritage / High-Fineness
karat_reference.durability_profile: 91.67% pure gold; suited for plain bands or protective bezel settings rather than thin claw prongs.

karat_reference.label: 24K Pure Investment Gold
karat_reference.durability_profile: 99.99% elemental Au; malleable — suitable for substantial plain bands (>=2mm thick), not tension or thin prong settings.

standards_sources.title: FTC Consumer Advice — Buying Platinum, Gold, and Silver Jewelry
key_takeaways: Defines 24-karat purity scale (14K = 14 parts gold, 10 parts alloy) and requires trademark stamp beside any quality mark.
Distinguishes solid karat gold from hollow gold and from plated, gold-filled, rolled gold plate, gold overlay, and vermeil (gold over sterling silver).
Advises buyers to get karat weight, gram weight, and return policy in writing before purchasing.

standards_sources.title: 16 CFR Part 23 — Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries
standards_sources.authority: Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (NARA / FTC)
standards_sources.citation: 16 CFR Part 23 (incl. § 23.3 Gold, § 23.4 Vermeil, § 23.7 Rhodium, § 23.8 Multi-Metal, § 23.10 Quality Marks)
key_takeaways: 16 CFR § 23.3: unqualified 'Gold' means fine (24K) gold through and through; a gold alloy must carry its karat designation immediately before the word 'Gold' and with equal conspicuousness; hollow-centred articles should not be marked 'solid'. There is NO 10-karat floor for calling a gold alloy 'karat gold' — § 23.3(c)(1) itself gives '9 Karat Gold' as acceptable — 10 karat survives only as the minimum fineness for plating, gold-filled and vermeil (§ 23.3(c)(2)-(3), § 23.4(b)).
16 CFR § 23.4: Vermeil requires sterling silver (>=92.5% Ag) coated with >=2.5 microns of >=10K gold — never solid gold.

16 CFR § 23.7: it is unfair or deceptive to fail to disclose a surface-layer application of rhodium on a product marked or described as precious metal — the relevant rule for rhodium-plated white gold. 16 CFR § 23.8: where a product contains more than one precious metal, the relative quantity of each must not be misrepresented, and metals should be listed from greatest to least by weight (e.g., an 18K shank with platinum prongs).

15 U.S.C. § 297(b) (National Stamping Act): a quality mark indicating gold or silver must be accompanied by the maker's registered trademark (or the maker's name), applied by the same means, in lettering at least as large, and as close as possible to the quality mark. § 297(b)(B) adds that where a multi-part article has parts of different quality, each other part must carry a matching quality mark. The FTC's consumer page states the practical version: don't buy a gold piece if the trademark is missing beside the karat mark.
16 CFR § 23.7: a surface-layer application of rhodium must be disclosed.
16 CFR § 23.10 (read 2026-10-23): a quality mark must be accompanied by the manufacturer's or dealer's registered trademark or name; § 23.9, by contrast, is the pewter section.
15 U.S.C. § 297(b) (read 2026-10-23): the trademark must be applied by the same means, in lettering at least as large as the quality mark and as close as possible to it.
standards_sources.correction_2026_10_23: The trademark rule was cited to § 23.9, which is the pewter section. It is § 23.10 ('Additional guidance for the use of quality marks'). Corrected after reading both sections on the eCFR page.

standards_sources.title: CFPB Official Guidance — Disputing Credit Card Charges (Fair Credit Billing Act)
key_takeaways: The CFPB page states: send a written billing-error notice within 60 calendar days after the charge appears on your statement; the card company then has 30 days to confirm receipt in writing.
12 CFR § 1026.13(c)(2) and 15 U.S.C. § 1666(a)(B) — not the CFPB FAQ page — set the outer resolution limit: two complete billing cycles, and in no case later than 90 days after the notice.

Project guidance (not a CFPB statement): pay with a credit card rather than wire transfer, a peer-to-peer app, crypto or a debit card, because only the credit-card route carries the statutory billing-error dispute right.
standards_sources.correction_2026_10_23: The 90-day / two-billing-cycle limit was paraphrased as if the CFPB FAQ page said it; that page does not. It is now attributed to 12 CFR 1026.13(c)(2), and the card-only advice is labelled as this project's guidance.

standards_sources.title: GIA Gems & Gemology — Chemical Analysis in the Gemological Laboratory (EDXRF)
key_takeaways: Energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXRF) provides rapid, non-destructive elemental analysis from Na to U but measures only the shallow near-surface excitation depth.
Because XRF is surface-shallow, heavy plating or gold-on-gold plating can skew single-spot surface readings unless paired with mass/density and microscopic inspection.

standards_sources.title: GIA Lab Notes — Electroformed Gold Piece with Adhered 14K Hallmark Fraud Case
standards_sources.authority: Gemological Institute of America (GIA Carlsbad Laboratory)
key_takeaways: Item submitted as '14K solid gold' had a glued-on 14K hallmark disk over a wax/resin core coated with up to ~200 microns of electroformed gold.
Standalone surface XRF read 17.99K and 22.47K gold without detecting subsurface core! Fraud was caught by suspiciously low weight-in-hand + binocular microscope examination.
Proves why buyers MUST combine calibrated gram scale weight + microscopic hallmark/seam inspection + multi-spot XRF.

standards_sources.authority: U.S. Code (Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School)
standards_sources.title: 15 U.S.C. § 1666 — Correction of billing errors (Fair Credit Billing Act)
key_takeaways: § 1666(a): on receiving a written billing-error notice within 60 days of the statement, the creditor must send a written acknowledgement within 30 days (unless it resolves the dispute in that time).
§ 1666(a)(B): the creditor must correct the account or send a written explanation within two complete billing cycles, and in no event later than 90 days, after receiving the notice.
§ 1666(b)(3): a 'billing error' includes goods or services not accepted by, or not delivered in accordance with the agreement to, the cardholder.

checklist.title: Confirm Gold Purity in Karats (10K, 14K, 18K, 22K, or 24K)
checklist.requirement: Verify exact numeric karat fineness in both product title AND specification table. Under 16 CFR § 23.3, anything under 10K cannot legally be sold as karat gold in the U.S.
checklist.trap_caught: Caught TWO live listings on Sarraf (`SKU F1625` at $20,671 and `SKU 121987-.72P` at $2,858) where H1 title karat contradicts spec table karat (`18K` vs `14K`)!

checklist.title: Confirm Explicit 'Solid Gold' Construction — Reject Plated, Vermeil, Filled & Gold-Tone
checklist.requirement: Confirm the piece is solid karat gold throughout — NOT hollow, gold-plated, gold vermeil (>=2.5um gold over 925 silver), gold-filled, rolled gold plate, gold overlay, or gold-tone.
checklist.trap_caught: Caught Mejuri's `Organic Dome Nesting Ring Set` ($188) inside `/collections/diamond-rings`, whose copy literally contains the substring `'18k solid gold'` inside `'thick layer of 18k solid gold plated on 91% recycled sterling silver'`!

checklist.title: Verify Quality Hallmark AND Registered Maker's Trademark
checklist.requirement: Under the National Stamping Act (15 U.S.C. § 297), any karat stamp (`14K`, `585`, `18K`, `750`) MUST be accompanied by a registered manufacturer/seller trademark stamp (`MEJURI`, `MENE`, etc.). Request macro photos of inner-shank stamps.
checklist.trap_caught: Across all 21 solid-gold online listings audited, almost no retailer displays macro hallmark photography online — and GIA documented fake `14K` disks glued inside non-solid jewelry.

checklist.title: Obtain Documented Ring Metal Weight in Grams for YOUR Ring Size
checklist.requirement: Get net precious-metal gram weight in writing for the exact finger size ordered before checkout. Deduct gemstone weight (`1.00 ct = 0.200 g`) when computing pure gold mass.
checklist.trap_caught: Brilliant Earth, Blue Nile, Catbird, and Mejuri omit static gram weights on engagement settings, while Sarraf quotes wedding band weights at men's Size 10 (~12-18% heavier than women's Size 6).

checklist.title: Audit Multi-Metal Prong Heads & Plating Disclosures
checklist.requirement: Check whether prongs/basket use a different alloy than the shank (e.g., 14K white gold or platinum head on an 18K yellow gold band, or rhodium electroplating on white gold per 16 CFR §§ 23.7–23.8).
checklist.trap_caught: Caught Brilliant Earth `BE1199H6-18KY` (18K band + 14K white gold prongs) and Blue Nile `500000y` (18K band + Platinum prongs) advertised under single-karat titles.

checklist.title: Compare Asking Price Against Live Raw Fine-Gold Melt Value
checklist.requirement: Compute `Fine Gold (g) = Net Metal Weight (g) x (Karat / 24)` and multiply by dated spot gold (`$129.39/g` Kitco on `2026-10-22`). Plain machine-made solid bands cluster near `1.33x-1.50x` melt; any ring priced near or below `1.0x` melt is almost certainly hollow or plated.
checklist.trap_caught: Immediately flags $188 vermeil dual-band set as physically impossible for solid 18K gold (`5g` of 18K melt alone = `$485.23`), and exposes extreme designer markups.

checklist.title: Verify Seller Reputation, Physical Street Address & Live Support
checklist.requirement: Confirm a real verifiable street address, telephone/email customer service, independent reviews/complaints history, and transparent corporate identity before submitting payment.
checklist.trap_caught: Verified physical headquarters and published support channels across all 6 audited retailers on `sellers.html`.

checklist.title: Audit Return Window Start Trigger, Fees & Custom/Resized Exclusions
checklist.requirement: Confirm exact return window length, whether the clock starts at SHIPMENT or DELIVERY, restocking/shipping fees, missing lab certificate penalties, and custom/engraved/resized final-sale exclusions.
checklist.trap_caught: Menē gives only **7 days**; Catbird gives **20 days** (`$9` fee, international final sale); Blue Nile starts its 30-day clock on **SHIPMENT date** (`$150` missing cert fee); Sarraf voids warranty upon third-party resizing and charges `max($100, 10% of price)` for warranty replacement.

checklist.title: HARD STOP RULE: Walk Away If Independent Inspection + Return Is Barred
checklist.requirement: Order raw, UNENGRAVED, standard stock size first so the ring remains 100% refundable during independent testing. If a seller refuses returns after non-destructive inspection, DO NOT BUY.
checklist.trap_caught: Engraving or resizing at checkout immediately converts otherwise refundable rings at Blue Nile, Catbird, and custom settings at Brilliant Earth into non-returnable or fee-penalized orders.

checklist.title: Pay Strictly by Credit Card (FCBA Chargeback Protection)
checklist.requirement: Use a major credit card — never wire transfer, ACH, Zelle, debit card, cash app, or cryptocurrency — to retain statutory dispute rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act (60-day written dispute window).
checklist.trap_caught: Protects full purchase amount if assay or gram weight contradicts written product claims and seller stalls refund.

checklist.title: Archive Full Listing HTML/PDF, Written Weight Confirmation, Receipt & Certs
checklist.requirement: Save full-page timestamped PDF/screenshots of the product page, live chat/email gram-weight confirmation, invoice, and GIA/LBMA certificates before shipping.
checklist.trap_caught: Retailer prices and specs drift rapidly (e.g., Brilliant Earth setting jumped `$650 -> $850` between search cache and `2026-10-22` live page).

checklist.title: Immediate Post-Arrival Independent Jeweler Inspection + Multi-Spot XRF Test
checklist.requirement: Within 48 hours of delivery (TAGS INTACT, UNWORN, BEFORE RESIZING!), have an independent local graduate gemologist/jeweler: (1) weigh on calibrated 0.01g scale, (2) inspect hallmarks, prongs & seams under binocular microscope, and (3) run multi-spot EDXRF metal purity analysis.
checklist.trap_caught: Defeats single-point XRF spoofing from thick electroforming over resin/wax or 18K gold plated over 10K alloy documented by GIA Carlsbad Laboratory.

flagged_items.title: Incorrect Statement That 10K Is The Legal Minimum For 'Karat Gold' — Corrected Against 16 CFR 23.3(c)(1)
flagged_items.detail: The site previously described 14K as the 'lowest fine-gold content legally sellable as karat gold in the U.S. under 16 CFR § 23.3'. That is wrong for the current rule. Read live on 2026-10-23, 16 CFR 23.3(c)(1) lists '9 Karat Gold' and '9 Kt. Gold' among acceptable descriptions, and the 2018 revision of the Guides removed the former 10-karat threshold for the word 'gold'. The 10-karat figure that remains in Part 23 is a minimum fineness for PLATING: gold plate / gold filled / gold electroplate under 23.3(c)(2)-(3) and vermeil under 23.4(b). The cell was rewritten to say exactly that, and no dataset row was affected (no 9K row exists).
flagged_items.action: Corrected in data/catalog_a0be79d4.json; the karat table now states the market practice, the removal of the 10K threshold and the surviving plating floor, each traceable to the eCFR text.

flagged_items.item_ref: standards.html — eCFR summary bullets (16 CFR § 23.3 line)
flagged_items.title: Same 10K Myth Found In A Second Place After The Table Was Fixed — Plus Two Wording Fixes To § 23.7/§ 23.8 And The Chargeback Deadline
flagged_items.detail: Reading the Standards page line by line after the karat table was corrected showed the '10K is the legal minimum' myth repeated verbatim in the eCFR summary bullet. It is now replaced with what § 23.3 actually requires. Two further statements were tightened: (a) the § 23.7/§ 23.8 bullet conflated two different rules — § 23.7 requires disclosure of a rhodium surface layer, while § 23.8 requires metals to be listed from greatest to least by weight; (b) the chargeback bullet attributed the 'two billing cycles / max 90 days' resolution deadline to the CFPB page, which does not state it — that deadline is in 15 U.S.C. § 1666(a)(B), which is now cited and linked. The 60-day notice period and the 30-day acknowledgement are confirmed on the CFPB page itself.
flagged_items.action: Both legal bullets rewritten to match the regulation text; 15 U.S.C. § 1666 added as its own linked source card so the deadline is traceable.

flagged_items.title: Trademark/quality-mark rule was cited to the pewter section
flagged_items.detail: The standards page and this catalog cited '16 CFR § 23.9' for the rule that a quality mark must carry the maker's trademark. § 23.9 is 'Misrepresentation as to content of pewter.' The rule is § 23.10 'Additional guidance for the use of quality marks', which itself cites 15 U.S.C. § 297. Both sections were read on the eCFR page on 2026-10-23 and the citation was corrected. Nothing numeric changed.
flagged_items.action: No buyer action. Reading only: a regulation citation that looks convincing can still name the wrong section — check the section heading, not just the number.
